why: LANDED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 R5): `EmbeddedPublisher::publish(&self, msg: impl core::borrow::Borrow<M>)` takes the message borrowed or owned, as rclrs's `publish(impl MessageCow)` does, so an rclrs call site that hands its message over compiles unchanged. Both forms serialise immediately into the same stack buffer and put identical bytes on the wire (test `publish_takes_the_message_borrowed_or_owned`); the owned form only drops the message afterwards. What remains different is the buffer, not the argument: ours is a stack buffer of `DEFAULT_TX_BUF` bytes and `publish_with_buffer::<N>` picks another size at compile time, where rclrs allocates. PRIOR: ours is `EmbeddedPublisher::publish(&self, msg: &M)`; rclrs's takes the message by value (`impl MessageCow`) and serialises into a buffer it allocates. Ours serialises into a STACK buffer of `DEFAULT_TX_BUF` bytes (`packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/handles.rs`), and `publish_with_buffer::<N>(msg)` picks another size at compile time, because there is no allocator to size it at run time. It is `&M` rather than `M` because a no_std caller usually wants to keep the message. CORRECTED 2026-10-25 (phase-515 W0): this row used to say the caller passes the buffer (`publish(&self, msg: &M, buf: &mut [u8])`); that argument is gone, and only `&M` against by-value still differs at the call site. This is the `no-allocator` constraint at the hottest call in the API.
